new.name: Gantt bar labels and overlay line merged into table rows as garbled dates
new.page_shows: A schedule table on the left and a Gantt chart on the right; the bars carry date labels (e.g. 11-May-23 ... 18-May-23) and a red data-date line runs through them. Table Current Finish for the row is 18-May-23.
new.why_it_matters: The chart's own labels are read as extra table columns, truncated at the chart edge, and the line through them changes digits: 18-May-23 becomes a valid-looking 18-May-21 (two years earlier), other dates become nonsense. A scheduling query over the table gets wrong dates with nothing to mark them as chart annotations.
new.lesson: Treat the Gantt area as a chart region: do not OCR it into table cells; keep only the table columns, or flag the chart as a picture with its labels unattached.

new.name: Zero shown as a dash is dropped, leaving an empty cell
new.page_shows: Rows such as Materials & Supplies, Transmission Line Pack, Prepayments, Other each show '$ -' (zero) in the Initial Annual Forecast column, and the Deferrals row '$ -'.
new.output_says: | Materials & Supplies | Input |  |  |  |  and  | Deferrals (as Applicable) |  |  |  | $ |
new.why_it_matters: A reported zero becomes an empty cell, indistinguishable from 'not reported'; the dollar sign alone survives on some rows and not others, so sums and checks (Total Working Capital = Sum L5 to L9) cannot be followed and zero vs missing is lost. The OCR keeps '$' but not the dash.
new.lesson: Keep dash placeholders as an explicit value (0 or '-') with its row; flag cells where only a currency sign was read.
